newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to ease hard currency controls.
newsitem.headline: Romania to ease hard currency controls.

text.p: Romania will ease stringent exchange controls imposed earlier this month by excluding most state companies and oil firms from the measures, Central Bank governor Mugur Isarescu said in a telephone interview.
Romania will once more allow companies to retain their hard currency holdings, he said.
The move appeared to be a response to Western alarm at the exchange controls, which had damaged credibility ahead of a drive to raise loans on the international market.
The exchange controls were originally introduced to generate a hard currency fund for much-needed energy imports.
"The hard currency fund will be set up solely based on market rules," said Isarescu. Only companies exporting products subsidised by the state would now contribute to the fund.
These include wheat, timber and vegetable oil exporters. Some 100 state companies will now be freed from the controls introduced in response to a severe hard currency squeeze.

State oil companies were finding it impossible to fund their imports ahead of Romania's harsh winter. It was not clear how the relaxation of the measures would affect their ability to find local hard currency sources to fund imports.

The hard currency controls were bitterly criticised when introduced and were seen as a political attempt to prevent a repeat of last year's currency crisis ahead of November 3 presidential and parliamentary polls.

The move lost Romania credibility with international institutions, already damaged by restricting the local forex market to four market-makers in March, which led the International Monetary Fund to hold back loan tranches.
